A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ShifTS research. All 17 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2, including Appendices A–E, are readable and support comparison of the text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments, baseline comparisons, and ablations in Section 4, Tables 1–4, and Figure 3, including additional results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the forecasting comparisons, ablations, mutual-information analysis, and appendix results.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same SAM construction, surrogate-feature prediction, aggregation MLP, RevIN normalization, losses, and training/testing procedures. The SAN substitution was already present in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate univariate forecasting with exogenous features on ILI, Exchange, ETTh1, ETTh2, ETTm1, and ETTm2. The ETTh1–Traffic illustration in Appendix C also remains unchanged. Newly cited benchmarks are not added evaluations.

E2.justification: The same six forecasting backbones are evaluated in Tables 1 and 4. Table 2 retains ERM, GroupDRO, IRM, VREx, EIIL, RevIN, N-S Trans., SAN, IRM+RevIN, EIIL+RevIN, and FOIL. The newly cited foundation models do not participate in reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix C retain the same preprocessing and split descriptions, forecasting horizons, lookback and decoder windows, MSE/MAE metrics, and temporal segmentation for environment labels. No new evaluation protocol or revised experimental setting is reported.

E4.justification: Both retain the Exchange 96-step component ablation, mutual-information versus performance-gain analysis, SAN substitution comparison, and dataset-shift visualization. Their questions, conditions, and evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report the same correlation p-value of 0.012 in Section 4.2. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4 match, and the plotted results are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains ShifTS MSE values of 0.668 on ILI and 0.470 on Exchange; Table 3 retains the ShifTS-with-SAN average MSE of 0.407.

T1.justification: Definitions 2.1–2.2 receive grammatical edits without changing their meaning. The mathematical assumptions, equations, objectives, and Appendix C.3 mutual-information calculation remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: SAM mitigates concept drift, temporal-shift mitigation is a prerequisite, and the model-agnostic ShifTS framework improves forecasting. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 retain the explanations involving horizon information, forecasting-backbone differences, and joint treatment of both shifts. Appendix E retains the lack-of-theoretical-guarantees limitation and discussion of alternative solutions. The added Appendix A material concerns related-work positioning.

D1.justification: The V100 32GB hardware disclosure, code/data access statement, baseline implementation sources, hyperparameter guidance, PatchTST MLP adaptation, and mutual-information computation details are retained. No additional reproducibility information is supplied.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds discussion of foundation-model scaling and multimodal/text-conditioned forecasting, with citations including GIFT-Eval, Chronos-2, Sundial, and Time-MMD, plus newer forecasting references. This broadens context while retaining the original positioning against invariant-learning and normalization approaches.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording edits to the distribution-shift definitions, rewrites and extends part of Appendix A, and updates acknowledgments and author/header text. The main narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–2 are enlarged, Table 3 and surrounding prose are reflowed, and the author block and conference header are reformatted. All figure images and table contents are retained; appendix pagination shifts without adding displays.

improvement.justification: The expanded Appendix A supplies useful context about foundation models and multimodal forecasting, while larger method diagrams and main comparison tables improve readability. These are limited gains: the method, empirical support, reproducibility information, and acknowledged limitations remain unchanged.
